reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the formation of isolated Pt/Pd sites, charge transfer to noble metals, and enhanced nitrobenzene adsorption and activity in PtPdCoCuNi HEA, but it does not address the key premise that low-temperature synthesis (restricted precursor mobility) is the cause of these features; the synthesis method is described as a one-pot solvothermal route without specifying low temperature or mobility control.
premises: Low-temperature synthesis inhibits precursor mobility and leads to a uniform, single-phase HEA nanostructure
This synthesis yields isolated Pt and Pd active sites within the HEA matrix
Charge transfer occurs from base transition metals (Co, Cu, Ni) to Pt and Pd
This charge transfer modulates the electronic structure to enhance reactant adsorption
The enhanced adsorption improves catalytic performance (e.g., nitrobenzene hydrogenation) compared to conventional catalysts
